items.title: Dara, Amoi and Kelat healthy, not abused at Japanese zoo — Taiping council
items.summary: Its president, Mohamed Akmal Dahalan, said the elephants — Dara, Amoi and Kelat — were in good health and had adapted well to their new surroundings since arriving in Japan in March. He said the latest reports from the zoo, alongside MPT's assessment, showed that all three elephants were active and in satisfactory overall condition. MPT also denies any allegations of neglect or abuse involving the elephants.

items.title: Today's news in pictures - Thursday, October 22, 2026
items.summary: MISSED what happened today? Here's a glimpse at what happened throughout the country in photographs. [[nid:1561576]] [[nid:1561575]] [[nid:1561574]] [[nid:1561573]] [[nid:1561572]] © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: Human Resources Ministry lodges reports over alleged meddling in TalentCorp review
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Human Resources Ministry has lodged several reports with the authorities over alleged attempts to interfere with an ongoing review and investigation at Talent Corporation Malaysia Bhd (TalentCorp). it said. The ministry said the review must proceed independently and transparently, without undue interference or influence.

items.title: Alleged Geng Suria leader, eight others charged as organised crime group members
items.summary: SUNGAI PETANI: Nine men were charged in the Sessions Court with being members of an organised crime group known as 'Geng Suria'. They were Thayalan, 28; A. Tana Balan, 30; Muhamad Rizwan Abd Jalil, 28; G. Sritharan, 39; B. Saranraj, 38; A. Simon, 34; G. Suria Prasad, 30, who is alleged to be the gang leader; A. Suresh, 52; and Kavines, 31. Lawyer S. Sagthiyaraj represented Saranraj and Thayalan, while lawyer Mohammad Naim Kamaruddin represented Sritharan, Simon and Tana Balan.

items.title: Indonesia channels US$68mil to tackle fires, haze
items.summary: JAKARTA: Indonesia has disbursed a second tranche of 1.235 trillion rupiah (about US$68 million) in central government aid to combat forest and land fires, with priority given to healthcare services for affected residents, a senior minister said today. Human Development and Culture Coordinating Minister Sugiono said the funds would be used to distribute face masks and portable oxygen supplies, establish recovery facilities and treat people suffering from acute respiratory infections. The aid will finance firefighting equipment, including protective gear, water pumps, hoses and peatland water injectors, as well as personnel deployment and logistical support, Sugiono said.

items.title: Saudi Aramco orders Dhahran headquarters evacuation as Houthi attacks intensify
items.summary: RIYADH: Saudi state oil company Aramco has told staff to evacuate its headquarters in Dhahran on the Gulf, six people with knowledge of the matter told Reuters on Thursday, as fighting between the world's largest crude exporter and Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis intensifies. The instruction to staff to evacuate the building and work remotely follows a wave of Houthi attacks on the kingdom, targeting the company and Saudi airports. Saudi authorities did not confirm the attack.

items.title: BNM extends repayment deferments to families of Nepal-China flood victims
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Repayment deferments have been extended to families of victims affected by the recent floods along the Nepal-China border, Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) said. In a statement, the central bank said banks and insurance and takaful operators (ITOs) had engaged with the affected families following a meeting between BNM and the victims' next of kin on Oct 12. "Affected families are encouraged to continue engaging directly with their respective banks and ITOs.

items.title: News@9: Today's top headlines - October 22, 2026 [WATCH]
items.summary: Zetrix yet to pay Transport Minister said Zetrix AI Bhd has yet to make any payment towards the RM314 million in outstanding government revenue. Haze pressure Malaysia will press Indonesia to take effective action against forest fires causing transboundary haze when the matter is raised at the upcoming Asean Foreign Ministers' Meeting. © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: Jawi appeals RM160,000 damages award to Siti Kasim over wrongful arrest
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The Federal Territories Islamic Religious Department (Jawi), and 22 others have appealed against a High Court ruling ordering them to pay lawyer and activist Siti Kasim RM160,000 in damages over her wrongful arrest and detention in 2016. "An honest mistake of law does not constitute misfeasance in public office," she said. Meanwhile, lawyer A. Saha Deva, representing Siti Kasim, whose full name is Siti Zabedah Kasim, argued that the High Court had properly considered the facts and applied the law.

items.title: Trump 'behind bars' in Teheran's latest anti-US propaganda stunt
items.summary: TEHERAN: Anti-American propaganda is a common sight on the streets of the Iranian capital, but authorities have gone a step further with their latest effort – a life-size jail cell with an actor playing US President Donald Trump languishing inside. The 3D art installation is proving a hit with locals, who have been stopping to take selfies as well as hurl abuse at Trump, who is accused by Teheran of war crimes during the Middle East war. A screen set up nearby shows messages denouncing US "war crimes."

items.title: TSH Resources says Indonesia operations unaffected by forest fires
items.summary: "Under the group's strictly enforced zero-burning policy, the use of fire for any field operations, including land preparation, new planting and replanting, is prohibited across the group," it said. The policy reflected the group's commitment to preventing land clearing by burning, in compliance with Malaysian and Indonesian laws, it said. The policy has been incorporated into the group's sustainability policy since May 2009, applies to all group companies and extends to its contractors and suppliers.

items.title: Taiwan issues warnings as Typhoon Champi nears
items.summary: TAIPEI: A powerful typhoon headed towards Taiwan on Thursday, triggering the cancellation of dozens of flights and prompting warnings for locals to prepare for heavy rain, strong winds and giant waves. Typhoon Champi is expected to sweep past Taiwan's northeast coast on Friday and Saturday as it moves towards China and Japan, Taiwan's Central Weather Administration (CWA) said. Champi has maximum sustained wind speeds of nearly 195km per hour, according to the latest update from the Joint Typhoon Warning Center.

items.title: Evergrande's US$46bil debt nightmare yields just 1pct recovery
items.summary: HONG KONG: China Evergrande Group's liquidators have recovered US$435.9 million from asset sales and loan recoveries so far, highlighting the challenge of repaying creditors with claims of about US$46 billion against the developer. The liquidators said they had raised the US$435.9 million through the sale of assets including aircraft, artwork and club memberships, as well as the settlement of loan receivables. They said 96 of the 107 artworks found at Evergrande's Hong Kong headquarters had been sold for US$28.8 million at a loss.

items.title: 14 cases of fallen trees reported across Seberang Prai after heavy rain
items.summary: BUTTERWORTH: Fourteen fallen tree incidents were reported in various parts on mainland Penang, with cleanup operations ongoing at several locations. The Seberang Prai City Council (MBSP) said works to clear fallen trees and other debris were being carried out to ensure public safety and minimise disruption to road users and residents. MBSP said the efforts were aimed at restoring affected areas, ensuring smooth traffic flow and safeguarding the well-being of residents.

items.title: Zetrix AI to hold sukukholders' meeting on covenant breach
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Zetrix AI Bhd will hold a meeting with sukukholders on Friday to discuss a proposed resolution to its covenant breach involving the shareholding of a substantial shareholder. In a filing with Bursa Malaysia tonight, the company said no payment default had occurred as at Thursday. "The sukuk trustee, Pacific Trustee Bhd, will convene a meeting with all the sukuk holders on Oct 23 to discuss the matter with a proposed resolution to address the cause of the breach, in relation to the shareholding of the substantial shareholder.

items.title: Malaysia gets Southeast Asia's only AMG One service hub
items.summary: MERCEDES-Benz Malaysia has invested RM2.2 million in a specialised service hub for the Mercedes-AMG One hypercar, making the nation the only location in Southeast Asia equipped to service the Formula 1-derived model. The facility will support owners across Southeast Asia, complementing an existing service hub in Japan. Mercedes-Benz Malaysia chief executive officer Martin Schulz said the facility builds on Malaysia's existing role in supporting the company's regional operations.

items.title: Court ruling strengthens PN's resolve ahead of Melaka polls, says Hamzah
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The High Court's decision to stay Perikatan Nasional's suspension and deregistration has strengthened the coalition's resolve ahead of the Melaka election. Parti Wawasan Negara (Wawasan) president Datuk Seri Hamzah Zainudin said the decision also offered renewed hope for PN to participate in the country's democratic process in a healthy and fair manner. "Wawasan welcomes the High Court's decision to stay the RoS notice concerning the revocation of PN's registration, allowing the coalition to use its logo in the upcoming Melaka state election.

items.title: Police bust alleged sex trafficking syndicate exploiting children, generating RM450,000 monthly
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 22 — Police have crippled ‘Geng Yunaa’, believed to be involved in 17 cases of child prostitution and trafficking for sexual exploitation, following ‘Ops Angel’ in the Klang Valley from Sept 24 to 26. He said two other group members were already being held at Kajang Prison and Henry Gurney School in Melaka for offences related to child trafficking and prostitution. “The group carried out sexual exploitation through prostitution by recruiting local teenagers, foreign nationals and underage children, who were exploited and made victims of prostitution in Selangor and Kuala Lumpur.

items.title: Thailand to tighten cannabis controls, propose tougher penalties
items.summary: BANGKOK: Thailand plans to tighten cannabis regulations and propose tougher penalties for violations as part of broader efforts to strengthen drug prevention and enforcement. Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul said the proposed amendments to the Narcotics Act concerning cannabis were discussed at the third meeting of the Office of the Narcotics Control Board (ONCB) this year on Thursday. He said the government would maintain a clear distinction between medical cannabis use and recreational consumption.

items.title: Ramanan questions Rafizi's claims over alleged RM9.5mil payment to corporate mafia
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: PKR vice-president Datuk Seri R. Ramanan has questioned Datuk Seri Rafizi Ramli's claims that he received RM9.5 million from businessman Victor Chin to resolve a corporate mafia issue. Ramanan said it had been seven months since the allegation was made, but Rafizi had yet to present any evidence. He also criticised Rafizi for allegedly making unsubstantiated statements and subsequently seeking public donations to cover legal costs after losing court cases.

items.title: Fires rage, haze spreads as Indonesians pray for rain
items.summary: SURABAYA: Indonesian schoolchildren prayed for rain on Thursday as another firefighter lost his life battling drought-fuelled blazes consuming forests and peatlands and blanketing parts of Southeast Asia in a sickening haze. The resulting haze has sickened hundreds of thousands in Indonesia and reached as far as Malaysia, Singapore and East Timor. In East Java, where fires have ravaged several regencies and conservation areas including Mount Bromo and the Baluran National Park, the governor urged communities to come together to "pray for rain."

items.title: Marine & General cautiously bullish about upstream outlook
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Marine & General Bhd maintains a cautiously optimistic outlook for its upstream division, underpinned by long-term contracts for its 60-metre anchor handling tug supply (AHTS) vessels. The outlook is also supported by an expected gradual recovery in Malaysia's exploration and development activities between 2026 and 2028. Following its 29th annual general meeting (AGM) held earlier today, the company said the ageing regional offshore support vessel (OSV) fleet.

items.title: Ringgit ends easier against greenback, major currencies ahead of FOMC meeting
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit closed lower against the greenback and other major currencies on Thursday as investors remained cautious ahead of next week's two-day US Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting. This came amid a decline in US Treasury yields and the US Dollar Index (DXY). At 6pm, the ringgit eased to 4.0815/0850 against the greenback from Wednesday's close of 4.0790/0825.

items.title: Suspect in MCBA officer's murder remanded for another seven days
items.summary: Negri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad said the suspect's initial remand, which began on Oct 16, expired today. "The initial remand expired today. Police applied for an extension at the Seremban magistrate's court, which granted another seven days until Oct 29," he said when contacted.

items.title: Gold futures end lower, in line with US Commodity Exchange losses
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Gold futures on Bursa Malaysia Derivatives closed lower on Thursday, tracking losses on the US Commodity Exchange. At the close, the October 2026 contract eased to US$4,085.30 per troy ounce from US$4,126.10 on Wednesday and the November 2026 contract decreased to US$4,101.90 from US$4,142.70 yesterday. The December 2026, January 2027, February 2027 and April 2027 contracts all edged down to US$4,117.90 per troy ounce from US$4,158.70 previously.

items.title: Petronas expands global two-wheeler reach through UM Motorcycles pact
items.summary: PETRONAS Lubricants International (PLI) has partnered UM Motorcycles to supply motorcycle lubricants across selected markets in Asia Pacific, Europe, Africa and Latin America, expanding its global reach in the two-wheeler segment. Under the agreement, PLI will supply selected products from its Petronas Sprinta range to UM Motorcycles' distributors and aftersales dealer networks, with the initial rollout beginning in Asia this month. It is aimed at strengthening aftersales support and customer engagement across UM Motorcycles' international network.

items.title: Viral Porsche road bully jailed five days, fined RM10,000 for dangerous driving
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, Oct 22 — A Porsche Cayenne driver was sentenced to five days in prison and fined RM10,000 by the Magistrate’s Court here today after pleading guilty to dangerous driving of the luxury car on a highway near Bandar Kinrara, which had gone viral on social media. Magistrate Nur Natasya Mohtaruddin, who handed down the sentence against Woo Hong Jiang, 56, ordered the man to serve his prison term starting today, alongside a five-year disqualification of his driving license and six months’ imprisonment if he fails to pay the fine. Deputy Public Prosecutor Adriana Maisarah Mohd Farid requested a heavy sentence, taking into account that dashboard camera (dashcam) footage showed the accused was a road bully who drove dangerously and whose actions could have caused an accident, noting also that the case had gone viral.

items.title: MCMC warns against sharing Kuching school violence footage involving teen, cautions of legal action
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 22 — The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) urges individuals who have uploaded or shared video footage of an incident involving a dangerous weapon at a school in Kuching, Sarawak, to immediately delete the content. The Commission further cautioned that disclosing the identities of children may constitute a violation of Section 15 of the Child Act 2001 (Act 611). “The dissemination of such content may also be subject to action under Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998 (Act 588), should it contravene the provisions of the law,” the statement read.

items.title: Queen donates 376,000 face masks to KL, Putrajaya schoolchildren
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Her Majesty Raja Zarith Sofiah, Queen of Malaysia, has donated 376,000 face masks to schoolchildren in Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya to help protect them from the haze. Also present were Grand Chamberlain of the Royal Household Datuk Azuan Effendy Zairakithnaini, Yayasan Raja Zarith Sofiah Negeri Johor chief executive officer Hishamuddin Abdul Rahim, and Education Ministry Deputy Director (Student Affairs Management) Hirudin Mohit. She also donated 200,000 face masks to Malaysian motorcyclists commuting to work in Singapore amid the haze affecting Johor.

items.title: MARKET PULSE PM OCT 22, 2026 [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia's key index reclaimed the psychological 1,600 level on Thursday supported by bargain hunting activities amid a cautious environment. The 30-stock index ended nearly six points higher at 1,608. KFArc0xR_FY © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: Telegram-based prostitution, human trafficking syndicate raking in RM5.4mil a year busted
items.summary: Federal Criminal Investigation Department director Datuk M Kumar said the group, known as Geng Yunaa, operated through the 'KLSELANGORFL' channel, offering an estimated 20 to 30 sex workers a day. "Based on this estimate, the group could generate RM15,000 a day," he said in a statement. Kumar said the group, comprising 10 members, had been active since early 2024 and recruited local teenagers, foreigners and underage children for sexual exploitation through prostitution in Selangor and Kuala Lumpur.

items.title: Samsuri rallies Perikatan machinery for Melaka polls after court freezes RoS deregistration
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 22 — Perikatan Nasional (PN) chairman Datuk Seri Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar has welcomed a High Court ruling granting an interim stay against the Registrar of Societies’ (RoS) decision to deregister the coalition, saying it will now direct its full electoral machinery towards the Melaka state election. “PN remains steadfast, and this struggle will continue,” he said, offering gratitude to supporters for their prayers and commending the coalition’s legal team for securing the urgent court intervention. Earlier today, High Court Judge Datuk Azizan Md Arshad allowed PN’s leave application to stay the RoS order revoking the coalition’s corporate registration pending the final disposal of its substantive judicial review challenge.

items.title: Anthony Loke backs local transport apps with open data on train schedules, passenger numbers
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 22 — Local application developers can leverage open public transport data to help commuters plan their journeys more conveniently, Transport Minister Anthony Loke said. He said the Transport Ministry (MoT) had adopted an open data policy several years ago, allowing interested parties to access the information to develop public transport applications. “Data under the ministry’s purview mainly relates to public transport, while road-related data involves other agencies, including the Works Ministry and the Public Works Department.

items.title: Stolen luxury goods, devices, put up for sale after Paris looting [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Luxury goods looted from high-end boutiques in Paris are being resold on the streets, with videos showing designer handbags, watches and tech products from ransacked stores circulating online amid the unrest in France. Footage from the haul also drew reactions from social media users, with some questioning whether the looters could be traced through the stolen tech devices. user geezy101_ commented.

items.title: High Court stay gives PN room to prepare for Melaka election
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Perikatan Nasional will focus on strengthening its preparations for the Melaka election after the High Court today stayed the Registrar of Societies Malaysia's (RoS) action to cancel the coalition's registration. Its chairman, Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar said PN was grateful for the decision and maintained that it was on the right track in defending its rights through legal channels. He said efforts by those seeking to "erase" PN would not weaken the coalition's resolve, adding that it would remain steadfast and continue its struggle.

items.title: MACC chief urges MCMC staff to expose misconduct and reject abuse of power
items.summary: Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) Chief Commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said MCMC staff should have the courage to report any abuse of power or unlawful instructions through official channels. Abd Halim said MCMC’s integrity programmes showed that both its senior management and staff were committed to strengthening accountability. The MCMC 2026 Integrity and Audit Month closing ceremony, themed “Empowering Integrity, Strengthening Governance”, was held at the MCMC Auditorium in Cyberjaya today.

items.title: Two men in viral Bukit Antarabangsa police chase charged with dangerous driving, drugs and weapons offences
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 22 — Two men who went viral on social media after crashing into public vehicles while attempting to evade police in Bukit Antarabangsa were charged in three separate courts in Ampang today on various offences, including obstructing civil servants, possessing dangerous weapons and drugs. Private driver Muhammad Putra Zulfaiz Zaidi, 32, and mechanic Mohamad Danial Haiqal Kamal Arifin, 21, pleaded not guilty to all charges read before Sessions Court Judge Norshila Kamarudin and Magistrates Siti Nur Ain Ariffin and Tiong Wen Wen. Before Judge Norshila Kamarudin, the two friends were jointly charged with possessing dangerous weapons in a public place, namely a machete and a sickle, at Jalan Wangsa 5, Bukit Antarabangsa, at 11 am on Oct 11.

items.title: Police raid Melaka scam call centres targeting Chinese, Vietnamese victims, arrest 29
items.summary: MELAKA, Oct 22 — Police crippled the activities of two call center syndicates suspected of being involved in online non-existent investment scams and love scams through two separate operations around Melaka Raya and Ayer Keroh, here. Melaka Tengah District Police Chief ACP Halim Abas said that in the first operation on October 20, 14 Chinese nationals - comprising 11 men and three women aged between 21 and 52 - were arrested at four accommodation units in a hotel in Melaka Raya between 1pm and 3 pm. “Initial investigations found that the premises were suspected of being used as a call center operations hub for online non-existent investment scam activities targeting Chinese nationals.

items.title: Court of Appeal revokes bail for wheelchair-bound man charged with trafficking 6.2kg of cannabis
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 22 — The Court of Appeal today overturned a High Court decision that had released a wheelchair-bound man on bail pending the disposal of his drug trafficking trial. He held that the High Court judge erred in applying Section 388 of the Criminal Procedure Code to allow bail when there is an express law dealing with bail for drug trafficking offences. The court ordered the RM150,000 bail deposited to be returned and revoked all previously imposed bail conditions.

items.title: Thunderstorms to lash Klang Valley, Penang, and six other states tonight
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 22 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a severe thunderstorm warning, forecasting heavy rain and strong winds across several states and federal territories until 9 pm today. Issued at 5:50 pm, the alert covers the entire Klang Valley, including Kuala Lumpur, Selangor, and Putrajaya, alongside Penang. Meanwhile, Perak is set to take a battering, with alerts plastered across Kerian, Selama, Larut Matang, Manjung, Bagan Datuk, Perak Tengah, Hilir Perak, Kampar, Kinta, and Kuala Kangsar.

items.title: EC opens 30-day review of September 2026 supplementary electoral roll
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 22 — The Supplementary Electoral Roll for September 2026 (DPT BLN9/2026) will be open for review for a period of 30 days, starting today until Nov 20, said Election Commission (EC) secretary Datuk Khairul Shahril Idrus. Additionally, the electoral roll contains 21,720 registered voters who have changed their electoral constituencies, as well as 4,805 voters who have undergone a change in their voter category or status. “The Election Commission (EC) urges citizens aged 18 and above as of the period between September 1 and September 30, 2026 as well as any registered voters who have applied to change their electoral constituency, voter category, or status, to verify their names in the Supplementary Electoral Roll (DPT) for September 2026 (DPT BLN9/2026).

items.title: Remand extended for suspect in AKPS officer’s murder at KLIA quarters
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Oct 22 — The man suspected of murdering his wife, a Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS) officer, at their residential quarters near Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) in Nilai on Oct 15 has had his remand extended for another seven days. Negeri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad said the suspect would remain in remand until Oct 29, while the case was being investigated under Section 302 of the Penal Code. “The extended remand period begins today and runs until Oct 29,” he told reporters.

items.title: Maintain Western technology for DNB, says MP
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 22 — Wawasan information chief and Machang MP Wan Ahmad Fayhsal Wan Ahmad Kamal has urged Putrajaya to maintain Digital Nasional Bhd’s (DNB) Western technology stack, saying it is needed to balance the growing role of Chinese technology in Malaysia’s 5G and AI infrastructure. He said DNB’s Ericsson-based network was now Malaysia’s main Western technology counterweight, following U Mobile’s selection of Huawei for the country’s second 5G network. Wan Fayhsal said Malaysia should not allow one technology ecosystem to become dominant across its critical digital infrastructure.

items.title: Five days’ warning: New Malaysian model forecasts haze before it hits
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 22 — Malaysia will introduce several transformative measures to strengthen efforts to tackle transboundary haze when it chairs the Sub-Regional Ministerial Steering Committee (MSC) on Transboundary Haze Pollution next year. Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Minister Datuk Seri Arthur Joseph Kurup said his ministry was conducting studies and drafting several new initiatives to ensure more effective and concrete action to address the recurring haze problem. “Malaysia will take over the MSC chairmanship next year, and we are studying and planning several new initiatives to strengthen Asean-level efforts to tackle the haze problem.

items.title: No drones without approval, Melaka police tell election candidates
items.summary: MELAKA, Oct 22 — Candidates and political parties intending to use drones during the Melaka State Election campaign must first obtain approval from the relevant authorities and cannot deploy the devices indiscriminately. Melaka police chief Datuk Dzulkhairi Mukhtar said drone operations were subject to regulatory controls by the relevant authorities, including the Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia (CAAM). “Even the police must obtain approval before using drones for operational purposes,” he told reporters after attending a briefing on the 16th Melaka State Election for political party representatives at the Melaka Police Contingent Headquarters here today.

items.title: Snip, snip, slip through? Wire fences cut at illegal crossings near Rantau Panjang-Thai border
items.summary: PASIR MAS, Oct 22 — Eleven police reports regarding damage to concertina wire fences at 13 illegal crossing points around Rantau Panjang were recorded between March 27 and October 12. Bukit Aman Internal Security and Public Order Department (PGA) Deputy Director Datuk Suzrin Mohamad Rodhi said the damage was believed to have been deliberately done to open up pathways for smuggling activities and cross-border crimes. Suzrin said his team constantly updates field information alongside the National Security Council and the police contingent regarding fence-cutting incidents in the border areas.

items.title: Court grants Perikatan stay on RoS deregistration, allows coalition to contest Melaka state polls
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 22 — The High Court here today allowed Perikatan Nasional’s (PN) application to stay the Registrar of Societies’ (RoS) decision to revoke the coalition’s registration pending the outcome of its judicial review. Judge Datuk Azizan Md Arshad also granted PN’s application to stay the enforcement of an RoS notice suspending all activities of the political coalition. The decision allows PN to continue its political activities, including contesting the Melaka state election scheduled for November 14.

items.title: Iran warns it will hit US bases if Hormuz ship escorts continue
items.summary: TEHRAN, Oct 22 — Iran’s Revolutionary Guards on Thursday threatened to strike American bases across the Middle East if the US military continues to escort ships through the Strait of Hormuz. “The US military must know that if this trend continues, the conflict will extend to its bases in the region,” the Guards, the ideological arm of Iran’s military, said in a statement on their Sepah News website. It regularly attacks ships that attempt to navigate the strait without its authorisation.

items.title: Do Malaysians know MA63? Communications Ministry may run a study to find out
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 22 — The Communications Ministry is considering conducting a dedicated study to gauge public understanding of the Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63) and the history of Malaysia’s formation. Deputy Communications Minister Teo Nie Ching said neither the ministry nor its agencies, including the Malaysian Information Department (Japen), had conducted a baseline study for this purpose. “At present, neither RTM nor Japen has conducted a survey to measure public understanding of MA63 and the formation of Malaysia.

items.title: Pay up or go to jail: 43 fined for using other people’s Malaysian ID cards in Johor Bahru
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Oct 22 — A total of 43 individuals, including three Malaysians, were fined between RM1,000 and RM9,000 by three Magistrates’ Courts here today for using forged identity cards or copies of identity cards belonging to other people. Of the total, 35 were charged with using copies of other people’s identity cards, while the remaining eight were charged with using forged identity cards as personal identification documents. The accused, aged between 18 and 49, comprised three Malaysians and foreign nationals from Indonesia and the Philippines.

items.title: MyEG suspension to continue as RM314m outstanding payment remains unsettled, says Loke
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 22 — Transport Minister Anthony Loke Siew Fook today said the outstanding payment MyEG Services Bhd (MyEG) owes the government has yet to be settled, following the suspension of the company’s services as a Road Transport Department (JPJ) collection agent earlier this month. MyEG is a digital and e-government services provider that was previously tasked with collecting JPJ-related payments. He said the suspension had not disrupted public access to JPJ services, as motorists could continue using alternative channels, including the MyJPJ application, to access their information and carry out transactions.

items.title: Haze row: Malaysia to take transboundary pollution to Asean meeting in Manila
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 22 — Malaysia urges Indonesia to take firm and effective action to tackle fires contributing to transboundary haze pollution, which is affecting air quality and public well-being in Malaysia. Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Minister Datuk Seri Arthur Joseph Kurup said Malaysia respected its good diplomatic relations with Indonesia but reserved the right to demand appropriate action to ensure its people could enjoy clean air. “Malaysia’s stance is clear.

items.title: TalentCorp business as usual, says HR Ministry, as it lodges reports on alleged interference
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 22 — The Human Resources Ministry (Kesuma) has lodged several official reports with the authorities over alleged attempts to interfere with an ongoing review and investigation at Talent Corporation Malaysia Berhad (TalentCorp). In a statement today, the ministry said the alleged interference involved spreading misleading information, influencing individuals within the agency, and diverting attention from matters under scrutiny. It said such actions could undermine the integrity and independence of the review and investigation.

items.title: Kuching school attack probe ongoing, police to hold press conference on Oct 27
items.summary: KUCHING, Oct 22 — Police are gathering and verifying information as investigations into the alleged attack on a female teacher at an international school here yesterday morning continue. According to the Sarawak Police Contingent Headquarters, the investigation team is carrying out various investigative measures to ensure the accuracy of the information obtained. Yesterday, acting Sarawak Police Commissioner DCP Saifullizan Ishak said police received a report of the incident at 8.03am via the MERS 999 emergency line.

items.title: Loke welcomes RM5m Masjid Jamek LRT makeover, wants stations to drive local economy
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 22 — Transport Minister Anthony Loke Siew Fook today welcomed a RM5 million beautification project at the Masjid Jamek LRT station, saying the busy interchange should be more than a transit point and help drive economic activity and tourism in the capital. Transport Minister Anthony Loke during the launch of the LRT Masjid Jamek Station Beautification Project in Kuala Lumpur October 22, 2026. Transport Minister Anthony Loke poses for a picture during the launch of the LRT Masjid Jamek Station Beautification Project in Kuala Lumpur October 22, 2026.

items.title: Bandar Kuching MP urges public to stop sharing Kuching school attack videos, warns of copycat effect
items.summary: KUCHING, Oct 22 — Bandar Kuching MP Dr Kelvin Yii Lee Wuen has urged the public and the media to stop sharing videos of a school violence incident in Kuching, warning that such exposure can lead to a copycat effect. “I appeal to everyone, including the media, to stop sharing videos, images, notes or details of this act,” Dr Yii said in a statement. Dr Yii also pointed to a troubling rise in violent incidents involving students since the killing of a student in Bandar Utama in October 2025.

items.title: RM1,000 aid lands just in time for Deepavali for 400 Negeri Sembilan taxi drivers
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Oct 22 — The RM1,000 special financial assistance from the Madani Government has brought relief to more than 400 taxi and hire car drivers in Negeri Sembilan, particularly those celebrating Deepavali, by helping them prepare for the festival, Transport Minister Anthony Loke said. He said the aid would help reduce recipients’ financial burden, allowing them to meet the costs of Deepavali preparations and their families’ daily needs. “I promised earlier that the assistance would be delivered before Deepavali.

items.title: Nine charged with being members of ‘Geng Suria’ crime group in Sungai Petani
items.summary: SUNGAI PETANI, Oct 22 — Nine men were charged in the Sessions Court here today with being members of an organised crime group known as the ‘Geng Suria’. They are Thayalan, 28; A. Tana Balan, 30; Muhamad Rizwan Abd Jalil, 28; G. Sritharan, 39; B. Saranraj, 38; A. Simon, 34; G. Suria Prasad (alleged to be the gang leader), 30; A. Suresh, 52; and Kavines, 31. Lawyer S. Sagthiyaraj represented Saranraj and Thayalan, while lawyer Mohammad Naim Kamaruddin represented Sritharan, Simon, and Tana Balan.

items.title: Malaysia eyes bigger role in Turkmenistan’s oil and gas sector
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 22 — Malaysia is strengthening its energy partnership with Turkmenistan to unlock new commercial opportunities for companies, particularly in higher-value oil and gas services, technology and specialised engineering, said Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir. “Our companies are ready to work with Turkmenistan partners not only as suppliers, but as long-term collaborators committed to local value creation,” the minister said in his remarks during the opening plenary of the Oil and Gas of Turkmenistan 2026 in Ashgabat. The three-day OGT 2026, which began on Oct 21, brought together 20 Malaysian oil and gas services and equipment (OGSE) companies, including Petroliam Nasional Bhd (Petronas), according to a statement by the Economy Ministry today.

items.title: Why your air quality app and the official API don’t match, environment minister explains in Parliament
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 22 — The Air Pollutant Index (API) readings issued by the Department of Environment (DOE) remain the government’s official reference for determining air quality and managing haze. Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Minister Datuk Seri Arthur Joseph Kurup said the official API was calculated based on the concentrations of six major pollutants monitored around the clock through 68 automatic air quality monitoring stations nationwide. “Station operations include equipment maintenance, calibration, instrument performance checks and quality assurance procedures to ensure that the data used to calculate the official API are accurate and reliable,” he said during the Minister’s Question Time in the Dewan Rakyat today.
